skill.name: check-migration
skill.description: Checks Flyway migration files for naming, version conflicts, gaps, main branch conflicts, and basic SQL safety signals.
skill.summary: Review Flyway migrations before merge with file, version, and branch conflict checks.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline examples, and readable Japanese documentation. The skill describes fixed migration inspection commands and report formatting, with no evidence of prompt injection, obfuscation, dynamic command construction, credential access, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The workflow includes git fetch origin, which contacts the configured remote.
remediation.suggestion: Document this side effect and ask the user before running git commands that contact remotes.

content.value_statement: Migration conflicts can break releases and database deploys. This skill guides checks for Flyway names, versions, main branch conflicts, and basic SQL safety.
actual_capabilities: Lists Flyway migration files under backend/src/main/resources/db/migration.
Identifies files that match the V number and description naming pattern.
Guides checks for sequential, duplicate, and missing version numbers.
Compares migration paths against origin/main for branch conflicts.
Checks basic SQL signals such as CREATE TABLE and IF NOT EXISTS.
Produces a structured completion report for migration status.
limitations: Does not run a full SQL parser or database engine validation.
Assumes the repository uses the documented migration directory path.
Requires a local git repository with an origin/main reference.
Only checks simple idempotency signals, not all rollback or data risks.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge Migration Review
use_cases.description: Check migration names, versions, and main branch conflicts before a pull request is merged.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Check
use_cases.description: Confirm that pending Flyway migrations are organized and ready for deployment review.

use_cases.title: Schema Change Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist for migration file hygiene during database change review.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Flyway migration files in this repository and report naming, version, and basic SQL issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before opening a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Review Versions Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Review migration version numbers for duplicates, gaps, and order problems. Do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against Main
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my branch migrations with origin/main and identify any conflicting version numbers or migration paths.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full migration checklist and produce a release-ready summary with blockers, warnings, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: Check a branch with three new Flyway migration files before merge.
output: Result: no duplicate versions and no main branch conflicts found.

output_examples.input: Review a migration set with a repeated version number.
output: Issue found: two files use version V011.
Re-run the check after updating the filename.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release check for pending schema changes.
output: Next step: confirm whether the gap is intentional before release.

best_practices: Run the checklist before merging database changes.
Review git remote operations before allowing them to run.
Pair this skill with database-specific SQL validation for critical releases.
anti_patterns: Do not treat basic string checks as full SQL validation.
Do not ignore duplicate migration versions because files are on different branches.
Do not run remote git commands without understanding the repository context.

faq.question: What migration format does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects Flyway versioned migration files using a V number, two underscores, and a description.

faq.question: Can it validate every SQL dialect?
faq.answer: No. It performs simple SQL signal checks and should be paired with dialect-specific validation.

faq.question: Does it modify migration files?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reviews files and reports findings.

faq.question: Why does it compare with origin/main?
faq.answer: The comparison helps find migration version conflicts introduced by parallel branch work.

faq.question: Does it work outside the documented directory?
faq.answer: It is written for backend/src/main/resources/db/migration and may need adjustment for other layouts.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
